summary: Downscale a STILL to at most a target height, preserving aspect and the container (a PNG keeps its alpha, a JPEG stays a JPEG), so a browser-sized proxy exists for a still that lives only at the durable address. Never upscales.

parity.note: Deterministic for a fixed ffmpeg build: one decode, one bicubic scale, one still-image encode at a pinned quality over identical input bytes emits identical output bytes. tests/test_op_media_image_scale.py asserts the argv is a pure function of (params, paths) so a drift shows as an argv diff rather than as mystery-different pixels. WHY A SECOND OP and not a `kind: image` on media.scale: an op input has ONE kind, and media.scale's argv is video by construction (encoder profile, yuv420p, faststart, audio) — a still needs none of it and must keep its own container. The pre-existing box-side resize (preview_proxy.proxy_img) is the same ffmpeg spelling; this is that resize where the bytes actually are (STILL_SEAM_GAP).

height.description: Ceiling height in pixels: the still is scaled to min(height, its own height) with the width following its aspect (-2 = nearest even). GEOMETRY, the same class of fact as media.scale's `height`; the clamp lives here because only the pod holds the file open.
